sources.institution: Library of Congress, Congressional Research Service (public report mirror)
sources.title: Puerto Rico: A Chronology of Political Status History, 97-526, 1998
sources.usage: Body read: Introduction and chronology: 1900 Foraker civil government; Jones Act 2 March 1917 elected House/Senate; 1947 elective-governor legislation; 1952 proclamation and republican constitution. 1948 first-governor service and July 1950 date inconsistencies not used for precise transition dates.

sources.title: Swedish Caribbean Colonialism: About the project
sources.usage: Body read: Project body identifies Swedish colonial Saint-Barthélemy during 1784–1878 and later transfer to France; archive scope, not a modern sovereign-state fallback.

sources.institution: French Ministry responsible for Overseas Territories, François Seners
sources.title: Saint-Martin, Saint-Barthélemy: quel avenir pour les îles du nord de la Guadeloupe?, 1999
sources.usage: Body read: PDF pages 5–8: French/Dutch partition; Swedish administration and French attachment 16 March 1878; practical near-absence of colonial administration 1880–postwar. French-side Saint-Martin cannot be assigned to an ambiguous whole-island raw identity.

sources.title: Saint Christopher and Nevis, 5 May 1983, HC Deb vol 42
sources.usage: Body read: Minister’s historical opening, columns 515–516: Saint Christopher and Nevis united with Anguilla by federal Act 1882; associated statehood only 1967. No 1882 commencement-day inference.

sources.title: Leeward Islands Act 1871
sources.usage: Body read: Original Act sections 2–8 lists Saint Christopher and Nevis as separate presidencies; used to flag pre-union collective raw label, not to project six-presidency composition after 1882.

sources.title: Constitutional Development
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body 1808–1951: Crown-colony Orders-in-Council, 1816/1832 councils, Windward administrator, 1924 letters patent/1925 elected council, reserve powers 29 October 1936, adult-suffrage framework 1951. Later modern independence text not projected.

sources.institution: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, House of Assembly
sources.title: Historical Perspectives of the Legislature
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: 1936 administrator-presided council and elected/nominated/official members; 1951 new constitution and adult suffrage; 1956/1959/1960 subsequent reforms reviewed but left outside accepted early framework.

sources.institution: US Department of the Interior, Office of Insular Affairs
sources.title: U.S. Virgin Islands: History and Political Status
sources.usage: Body read: History body: prior Danish islands, US purchase 1917, citizenship 1927, Interior authority 1931, Organic Act 1936 and revised Act 1954. Modern leadership section excluded.

sources.title: Evolution of a Nation: Trinidad and Tobago at Fifty, 2012
sources.usage: Body read: PDF pages 27–31 and 71–77: early Council of Advice; Governor and nominated councils before 1925; elected minority from 1925; 1945 franchise and 1950 reforms. Counts vary and are not generalized across decades.

sources.institution: Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Legal Affairs
sources.title: Trinidad and Tobago Order in Council 1888
sources.usage: Body read: Two-page original historical Order, clauses 1–3: united colony effective 1 January 1889; Tobago councils ended; Governor instructions extended. 2012 compilation date not treated as a contemporary rule.

sources.title: Antilles françaises research guide
sources.usage: Body read: Historical colonial administration section 1815–1946 and Martinique territorial archives; no modern mainland government projected during the Second World War.

sources.title: Échos de la départementalisation
sources.usage: Body read: Body records law 19 March 1946 making Martinique, Guadeloupe, Guyane and Réunion French departments, with contemporary newspaper evidence. Administrative implementation details omitted.

sources.institution: Government of The Bahamas, Constitutional Commission
sources.title: Report of the Constitutional Commission, July 2013
sources.usage: Body read: Section 5, PDF pages 47–50: Royal Governor, elected Assembly, nominated Council; 1909 separation of executive and legislative councils; internal self-government constitution only 1964. No modern Senate before 1964.

sources.title: History of Parliament, 15 January 2018
sources.usage: Body read: Full history body: 1831 union of Demerara, Essequibo and Berbice; Governor-presided Court of Policy through 1928, followed by new constitution. Article’s fixed membership numbers not generalized over 1831–1928.

sources.title: Guide to Government Documents, 2011
sources.usage: Body read: PDF pages 26–28 legislative holdings and page 38 chronology: appointed/elected chamber since 1883, 1944 adult suffrage, House of Representatives and Legislative Council after 1944, ministerial system 1953. Broad chronology’s 1938 end and 1957 full self-government shorthand not used as exact constitutional transitions.

sources.institution: UK Government, Turks and Caicos Islands Commission of Inquiry
sources.title: Final Report, 2009
sources.usage: Body read: PDF page 20 paragraph 1.21: Jamaica dependency from 1874. Accepted partial frame stops before 1959; report’s 1962 endpoint is not selected over differing accounts of 1959 separate administration.
